record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: Can untriggered two-particle correlations in events containing a 50–100 GeV jet, compared against minimum-bias events with a consistent centrality selection, provide insight into the interplay between jet-medium response and pure bulk-evolution effects?

evidence.quote:
Another measurement that could
provide insights into the interplay of jet-medium response and pure bulk evolution
effects is to analyse the untriggered two-particle correlations in events that contain
a 50-100 GeV jet and compare the result to the minimum bias one. One issue that
might complicate such a measurement is to find a consistent centrality selection, since
the requirement of a high momentum jet biases the event sample.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider relativistic heavy-ion collisions (e.g., Pb–Pb or Au–Au) in which a hot, dense quark–gluon medium is produced. Two complementary classes of soft-particle observables are commonly used:

(a) "Bulk-evolution" observables: untriggered two-particle angular correlations C(Δη, Δφ) constructed from all charged hadrons in a chosen low/intermediate transverse-momentum window, which reflect collective hydrodynamic flow harmonics v_n driven by event-by-event initial-state fluctuations.

(b) "Jet–medium response" observables: modifications of soft-particle distributions induced by the passage of a hard parton through the medium (e.g., medium-induced wakes, Mach-cone–like structures, and energy redistribution from quenched jets).

Formulate and answer the following question quantitatively. Let MB denote the minimum-bias event sample at a fixed centrality class c, and let J(c) denote the subsample of events at the same nominal centrality c that contain at least one fully reconstructed jet of transverse momentum p_T^{jet} ∈ [50, 100] GeV. Define the untriggered two-particle correlation function

  C_X(Δη, Δφ) = (1/N_X^{evt}) dN^{pairs}_X / d(Δη)d(Δφ),  X ∈ {MB, J(c)},

built from all charged hadrons (excluding constituents associated with the reconstructed jet) in a specified soft p_T range, and the difference

  ΔC(Δη, Δφ; c) = C_{J(c)}(Δη, Δφ) − C_{MB}(Δη, Δφ).

(i) Demonstrate, within a model that combines event-by-event hydrodynamic bulk evolution with a jet-energy-loss prescription that includes medium response, that ΔC carries information distinguishing pure bulk (initial-state fluctuation–driven) flow contributions from jet-induced medium response.

(ii) Address the centrality-selection bias: requiring a high-p_T jet biases the underlying event activity (multiplicity, ⟨p_T⟩, eccentricities) of the J(c) sample relative to MB at the same nominal centrality. Construct a centrality-matching procedure (e.g., based on a forward energy or multiplicity estimator decorrelated from the jet) such that, in the absence of a jet–medium response, ΔC vanishes within statistical precision; and quantify the residual bias.

(iii) Identify which features of ΔC (e.g., specific Fourier coefficients in Δφ, large-Δη ridge structure, near-side/away-side asymmetries) are most sensitive to jet-induced medium response as opposed to pure bulk evolution.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., reviews of minimum-bias jet systematics at RHIC, ALICE/ATLAS/CMS jet–hadron correlation analyses, and 2024–2025 studies on selection-bias effects in inclusive jets and energy correlators) continues to actively investigate how to disentangle jet-medium response from bulk hydrodynamic correlations and how to mitigate the centrality/selection bias induced by requiring a high-p_T jet. No definitive resolution of the proposed comparison between untriggered two-particle correlations in jet-tagged versus minimum-bias samples appears in the literature; the question remains an active open direction.

status_evidence.title: Minimizing Selection Bias in Inclusive Jets in Heavy-Ion Collisions with Energy Correlators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on minimizing selection bias in inclusive jets indicates the topic remains active.
status_evidence.claim: Selection-bias mitigation in jet measurements in heavy-ion collisions is an ongoing research problem.

status_evidence.title: Selection bias effects on high-pT yield and correlation measurements in O+O
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses selection-bias effects on high-pT yields and correlation measurements.
status_evidence.claim: Centrality/selection biases in jet-triggered correlation measurements are still being studied in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Review of minimum-bias jet systematics at RHIC
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews minimum-bias jet correlations at RHIC.
status_evidence.claim: Untriggered two-particle correlation analyses are an established but still-evolving probe of bulk and jet contributions.
